rule: Turn the one-line idea into a brief with vision, the user, MVP features, tech stack and a project structure outline before research.
why: The workflow starts with a written vision and MVP list, so later steps have something to test.
do: idea.md lists vision, who it is for, 3 to 5 MVP features, stack, folder outline, next step.
dont: Jumping from "a CRM for agencies" straight to screens.
source_quote: the ideation output has Project Vision, Key Features (MVP), Tech Stack, Project Structure Outline, and Next Step
check: check-record --base: the idea record has Vision, User, MVP, Out of scope and Next step headings with text under each.

rule: Write a project rules file (stack, folders, naming, tokens, banned patterns) before the first line of build code.
why: Step 8 of the workflow; rules keep many AI sessions consistent.
do: PROJECT-RULES.md with stack, folder map, naming, token file path and the ban list.
dont: Each build session re-deciding folder names and colors.
check: check-record --base: a ARCHITECTURE.md has Project rules with Stack, Folders and Banned lines.

rule: Run a security review against the OWASP Top 10 before shipping anything with accounts, forms or data.
why: Step 13 of the workflow; broken access control is the top web risk.
do: Ship check lists each OWASP item as checked, not applicable, or open.
dont: Shipping a login form with no note on access control or input handling.
source_quote: The OWASP Top 10 is the reference standard for the most critical web application security risks.
check: check-record --ship: the ship record has a Security section naming access control and input validation.

rule: Deploy every change to a preview URL and QA it there before production.
why: Steps 15 to 17: preview, QA, then production.
do: Ship record links the preview URL and the QA pass on it.
dont: Merging to main and testing on the live site.
source_quote: 14 CODE REVIEW, 15 PREVIEW DEPLOYMENT, 16 QA TESTING, 17 PRODUCTION DEPLOY
check: check-record --ship: the ship record has Preview and QA sections, QA lists the screens and states tested.

rule: Name what you will watch after launch: errors, latency, traffic and saturation, and who looks.
why: Step 18 of the workflow; the four golden signals are the minimum.
do: Ship record: "Errors: runtime logs daily. Latency: p95 page load. Owner: Altaz."
dont: Launching with no plan to see breakage.
source_quote: The four golden signals of monitoring are latency, traffic, errors, and saturation.
check: check-record --ship: the ship record has a Monitoring section with at least errors and an owner.

rule: Keep phone tap targets at least 44px and spaced apart, with main actions in thumb reach.
why: Small, crowded targets cause mis-taps (synsation_ Build for Good UX Pt 19).
do: Bottom action bar with 48px buttons and 8px gaps.
dont: Three 28px icon buttons touching in the top corner.
source_quote: small tap targets placed close together cause mis-taps; mind thumb reach

rule: Pick the loading pattern by context: skeleton for page or list loads with known layout, spinner only for short single actions.
why: synsation_ Pt 3; skeletons show structure and feel faster.
do: Leads table shows 8 skeleton rows while loading.
dont: A full-page spinner over the dashboard for every load.
source_quote: choose the loading pattern by context, skeleton screen vs spinner
check: check-record --base: every screen lists a loading state naming skeleton or spinner.

rule: If you use glass, keep text contrast at 4.5:1 over the busiest part of the background, and use it on one layer only.
why: Glass is returning (synsation_), but blur over busy media fails contrast.
do: One frosted nav over a calm photo, tested for contrast.
dont: Every card frosted over a gradient blob.
source_quote: Skeuomorphism to flat to glass history; glass is coming back
check: Is glass used on at most one layer, with readable text over the busiest part?

rule: For cursor, magnetic and trail effects, start from a maintained library example (Motion.dev, Anime.js) and add a reduced-motion path.
why: Resource post from @avani.codes; libraries handle timing and cleanup.
do: Magnetic button from a Motion example with prefers-reduced-motion off switch.
dont: Hand-rolled rAF cursor that never stops on reduced motion.
source_quote: Anime.js (animation engine), Motion.dev (UI animation and interaction examples, e.g. cursor effects, magnetic, trails)
check: check-ui premium-reduced-content passes with reduced motion.

rule: A heading must not name a color or tone that contradicts the background it sits on.
why: 1.3.1 bug: "One step is black" sat on a black band and read as a mistake.
do: "Here the band turns light" on a light band.
dont: "One step is black" on a #000 band.
source_quote: Nothing automated catches the wrong "One step is black" wording on a black band

rule: Keep a pinned scroll scene to at most 3 screens of scroll per pinned step, and never more than 6 screens total.
why: 1.3.1 hole: long pins feel stuck and nothing checked length.
dont: A hero pin that eats 12 screens of scroll.
